title: ~기에는 [gieneun] (For, in order to)
shortExplanation: Used to express a purpose or intention ('for', 'in order to').
longExplanation: '~기에는 [gieneun]' is a structure used in Korean to indicate that one is doing something for a particular purpose or end goal, similar to 'in order to' or 'for the sake of' in English. It highlights the reason for an action and what is required to achieve it.

examples.sentence: 토픽 시험을 통과하기에는 더 많이 공부해야 해요.
examples.romanization: Topik siheomeul tong-gwa-hagi-eneun deo mani gongbuhaeya haeyo.
examples.translation: I need to study more in order to pass the TOPIK test.

examples.sentence: 학교에 늦지 않기에는 아침 일찍 일어나야 돼요.
examples.romanization: Hakgyoe neujji anh-gieneun achim iljjik ireonaya dwaeyo.
examples.translation: You have to wake up early to avoid being late for school.

examples.sentence: 자동차를 사기에는 더 많은 돈을 모아야 해요.
examples.romanization: Jadongchareul sa-gieneun deo maneun doneul moaya haeyo.
examples.translation: You need to save more money to buy a car.

examples.sentence: 달리기 대회에서 이기기에는 매일 연습해야 합니다.
examples.romanization: Dalligi daehoe-eseo igi-gieneun maeil yeonseuphaeya hamnida.
examples.translation: You have to practice every day to win the running competition.

title: ~나 보다 [na boda] (It seems, looks like)
shortExplanation: Used to express an assumption or guess, like 'it seems' or 'looks like'.
longExplanation: '~나 보다 [na boda]' is a common grammar pattern in Korean for making inferences or guesses based on observation or context. It can be translated as 'it seems that...' or 'looks like...' in English. It does not express absolute certainty, only a plausible guess or assumption.

examples.sentence: 날씨가 좀 춥나 봐요, 외투를 입어야겠어요.
examples.romanization: Nalssiga jom chupna bwayo, oetureul ibeoya getseoyo.
examples.translation: It seems a bit cold, I should wear a coat.

examples.sentence: 그가 나를 좋아하나 봐요, 항상 나를 찾아요.
examples.romanization: Geuga nareul joahanabwayo, hangsang nareul chajayo.
examples.translation: It looks like he likes me, he always comes to find me.

examples.sentence: 후배가 일을 잘하나 봐요, 상사가 그를 칭찬하고 있어요.
examples.romanization: Hubaega ireul jalhanabwayo, sangsaga geureul chingchanhago isseoyo.
examples.translation: It seems the junior is doing his job well; the boss is praising him.

examples.sentence: 친구가 오늘 기분이 안 좋나 봐요, 얼굴이 우울해 보여요.
examples.romanization: Chinguga oneul gibuni an jo-nabwayo, eolguri u-ulhae boyeoyo.
examples.translation: It seems my friend is in a bad mood today; he looks depressed.

title: ~나요? [nayo?] (Isn't it?, right?)
shortExplanation: Used to confirm or get the listener's agreement or opinion.
longExplanation: '~나요? [nayo?]' is a colloquial way in Korean to seek the listener's confirmation or agreement, akin to saying 'Isn't it?' or 'Right?' in English. It invites the other person's feedback or concurrence, helping foster a cooperative tone in conversation.

examples.sentence: 오늘 날씨가 정말 좋은데, 외출하면 좋을 것 같아요, 그렇지 않나요?
examples.romanization: Oneul nalssiga jeongmal joheunde, oechulhamyeon joeul geot gatayo, geureochi annayo?
examples.translation: The weather is really nice today, it’d be great to go out, don't you think?

examples.sentence: 이 레스토랑의 음식은 맛있는데, 다음에도 여기에 또 오면 좋을 것 같아요, 그렇지 않나요?
examples.romanization: I resteorangui eumsikeun masinneunde, daeumedo yeogie tto omyeon joeul geot gatayo, geureochi annayo?
examples.translation: The food at this restaurant is delicious; it’d be nice to come here again next time, wouldn't it?

examples.sentence: 그 상황을 이해하지 못한 건 저만이 아니었을 건데, 그렇지 않나요?
examples.romanization: Geu sanghwang-eul ihaehaji mothan geon jeomani anieosseul geonde, geureochi annayo?
examples.translation: I doubt I was the only one who couldn't understand that situation, right?

examples.sentence: 그 영화는 재미있어서 다시 보고 싶을 것 같아요, 그렇지 않나요?
examples.romanization: Geu yeonghwaneun jaemiisseoseo dasi bogo sipeul geot gatayo, geureochi annayo?
examples.translation: That movie was really fun; I think I'd like to watch it again, wouldn't you?

title: ~남짓 [namjit] (About, around)
shortExplanation: Indicates an approximate number or amount (similar to 'about' or 'around').
longExplanation: '~남짓 [namjit]' is added after numbers to indicate an approximate quantity, similar to 'about' or 'around' in English. It suggests the total might be a bit more or a bit less than that number, providing a near approximation.

examples.sentence: 저는 이 책을 100페이지 남짓 읽었어요, 아직 많이 남아서 더 읽어야 할 것 같아요.
examples.romanization: Jeoneun i chaegeul baekpeiji namjit ilgeosseoyo, ajik mani namaseo deo ilgeoya hal geot gatayo.
examples.translation: I've read about 100 pages of this book; I still have a lot left, so I think I should read more.

examples.sentence: 여기서 서울까지는 100km 남짓 거리가 있어요, 차로 가면 1시간 정도 걸려요.
examples.romanization: Yeogiseo Seoul-kkajineun baek-kilomeeteo namjit georiga isseoyo, charo gamyeon hansigan jeongdo geollyeoyo.
examples.translation: It's about 100 km from here to Seoul; it takes around an hour by car.

examples.sentence: 오늘은 사람이 5000명 남짓 모여서 큰 축제를 즐겼어요.
examples.romanization: Oneul-eun sarami o-cheon-myeong namjit moyeoseo keun chukjereul jeul-gyeosseoyo.
examples.translation: About 5,000 people gathered today and enjoyed a big festival.

examples.sentence: 내가 지금까지 읽은 책은 대략 200권 남짓이에요.
examples.romanization: Naega jigeumkkaji ilgeun chaegeun daeryak i-baek-gwon namjisieyo.
examples.translation: So far, I've read about 200 books.

title: ~는 대로 [neun daero] (As is, the way it is)
shortExplanation: Used to express 'the same way', 'just as', or 'exactly like'.
longExplanation: '~는 대로 [neun daero]' can follow a verb stem or a noun to indicate 'the way it is done' or 'just as someone does something.' It emphasizes doing or perceiving something exactly as it is, or following a particular method without changing it.
formation:
1) Verb stem + 는 대로
2) Noun + (으)로 + 대로
(Note: actual usage varies depending on the part of speech.)

examples.sentence: 엄마가 집을 청소하는 대로 나도 똑같이 청소해야 돼.
examples.romanization: Eommaga jibeul cheongsohaneun daero nado ttokgati cheongsohaeya dwae.
examples.translation: I have to clean the house the same way my mom cleans it.

examples.sentence: 그는 원래 하던 대로 계속 동일한 일을 해 왔습니다.
examples.romanization: Geuneun wonrae hadeon daero gyesok dongilhan ireul hae watseumnida.
examples.translation: He has continued doing the same work in the way he originally did.

examples.sentence: 친구가 가르쳐준 대로, 그래서 라면을 만들었어.
examples.romanization: Chingu-ga gareuchyeojun daero, geuraeseo ramyeoneul mandeureosseo.
examples.translation: I made the ramen exactly the way my friend taught me.

examples.sentence: 그 예술가의 그림은 본래 모습 그대로 감상해야 해요.
examples.romanization: Geu yesulgaui geurimeun bonlae moseup geudaero gamsanghaeya haeyo.
examples.translation: You should appreciate that artist’s painting in its original state.

title: ~는 바와 같이 [neun bawa gachi] (Just like, as if)
shortExplanation: Used to compare two situations, meaning 'just like' or 'as if'.
longExplanation: '~는 바와 같이 [neun bawa gachi]' is used to highlight a similarity between two actions or states. '바' (roughly 'the situation' or 'the way') and '같이' ('like') combine to mean 'just like that situation.' It carries a nuance similar to 'as if...' or 'the way that...' in English.
formation: Verb stem + 는 바와 같이 / Noun + (인) 바와 같이

examples.sentence: 그는 마치 태어난 것처럼 눈을 감은 바와 같이 잠을 잤어요.
examples.romanization: Geuneun machi taeeonan geotcheoreom nuneul gameun bawa gachi jameul jasseoyo.
examples.translation: He slept as if he had closed his eyes the moment he was born.

examples.sentence: 학생들은 선생님의 설명을 이해하지 못해, 마치 외국어를 들은 바와 같았어요.
examples.romanization: Haksaengdeureun seonsaengnim-ui seolmyeongeul ihaehaji mothae, machi oegugeoreul deureun bawa gatasseoyo.
examples.translation: The students couldn’t understand the teacher’s explanation, as if they were listening to a foreign language.

examples.sentence: 그녀는 고생한 것처럼 피곤한 얼굴을 한 바와 같이 집에 왔어요.
examples.romanization: Geunyeoneun gosaenghan geotcheoreom pigonhan eolgureul han bawa gachi jibe wasseoyo.
examples.translation: She came home looking exhausted, as if she’d had a hard time.

examples.sentence: 시험에 떨어진 것처럼 그는 슬픈 얼굴을 한 바와 같이 방에 들어갔어요.
examples.romanization: Siheome tteoreojin geotcheoreom geuneun seulpeun eolgureul han bawa gachi bange deureogasseoyo.
examples.translation: He entered the room with a sad face, as if he had failed the exam.

title: ~는 편이다 [neun pyeonida] (Tend to)
shortExplanation: Used to express a habit, tendency, or general characteristic of someone.
longExplanation: The structure '~는 편이다' is used in Korean to express regular habits or tendencies. It is typically translated as 'tend to (do)', 'usually (do)', or 'often (do)'. It helps describe the usual or characteristic behavior of a person or situation.

examples.sentence: 저는 매일 아침 일찍 일어나는 편이에요, 아침에 여러 가지 할 일이 많아서 일찍 일어나야 해요.
examples.romanization: Jeoneun maeil achim iljjik ireonaneun pyeoniyeyo, achime yeoreo gaji hal iri manaseo iljjik ireonaya haeyo.
examples.translation: I tend to wake up early every morning, as I have many things to do in the morning.

examples.sentence: 그는 감정적인 사람이어서 분노를 쉽게 보이는 편이에요, 때로는 그의 표현이 과해 보일 수 있어요.
examples.romanization: Geuneun gamjeongjeogin saramieoseo bunnoreul swipge boineun pyeoniyeyo, ttaeroneun geuui pyohyeoni gwahae boil su isseoyo.
examples.translation: Because he is an emotional person, he tends to show his anger easily; sometimes his expressions can look excessive.

examples.sentence: 사춘기 시절에는 고민이 아무리 커도 부모님한테 말하기 쉽지 않은 편이에요, 그들이 이해 못할 것 같아서 말이죠.
examples.romanization: Sachungi sijeol-eneun gomin-i amuri keodo bumonimhante malhagi swipji aneun pyeoniyeyo, geudeuri ihae mothal geot gataseo malijyo.
examples.translation: During adolescence, no matter how big our worries are, we tend not to share them with our parents, thinking they won't understand.

examples.sentence: 집에서는 주로 한식을 먹는 편이에요, 한국 요리를 가장 잘하니까요.
examples.romanization: Jib-eseoneun juro hansigeul meokneun pyeoniyeyo, hanguk yorireul gajang jalhanikkayo.
examples.translation: At home, we tend to eat Korean food, because that's what I cook best.

title: ~는다는 것 [neundaneun geot] (The fact that)
shortExplanation: Used to express 'the fact that' or 'the meaning that' when referring to or summarizing someone's statement or idea.
longExplanation: The '~는다는 것' construction is used to convey or emphasize 'the fact that' something is stated or believed. It can summarize someone’s words, thoughts, or statements. It often appears in discussions to restate a point or highlight that a particular idea or fact is important.

examples.sentence: 그가 학교를 다닌다는 것은 정말 열심히 공부하고 있다는 걸 보여주는 증거예요.
examples.romanization: Geuga hakgyoreul danindaneun geoseun jeongmal yeolsimhi gongbuhago ittdaneun geol boyeo-juneun jeunggeo-yeyo.
examples.translation: The fact that he attends school shows that he is really studying hard.

examples.sentence: 우리가 서로를 이해한다는 것은 정말 중요한 관계를 만들어 가는데 필요한 일이에요.
examples.romanization: Uriga seororeul ihaehandaneun geoseun jeongmal jungyohan gwangyereul mandeureo ganeunde pilyohan iri-eyo.
examples.translation: The fact that we understand each other is necessary for building a really important relationship.

examples.sentence: 나는 내 친구가 큰 성공을 거두었다는 것을 알고 참 기뻤어요.
examples.romanization: Naneun nae chinguga keun seonggongeul geodueot-daneun geoseul algo cham gippeosseoyo.
examples.translation: I was very happy to learn the fact that my friend achieved great success.

examples.sentence: 그가 운동을 좋아한다는 것은 건강을 위해 노력한다는 것을 의미해요.
examples.romanization: Geuga undongeul johahandaneun geoseun geongangeul wihae noryeokhandaneun geoseul uimihaeyo.
examples.translation: The fact that he likes to exercise means that he's making an effort for his health.

title: ~는데 [neunde] (But, and, so)
shortExplanation: Used to connect two clauses in various contexts—often 'but', 'and', or 'so'.
longExplanation: '~는데' is a versatile connector in Korean. Its meaning depends on context—sometimes it indicates contrast (but), sometimes a sequential or related action (and/so). It can also be used at the end of a clause to invite further elaboration or explanation.

examples.sentence: 날씨가 추운데 외투를 안 입었어요. 병이 나겠어요.
examples.romanization: Nalssiga chunneunde oetureul an ibeosseoyo. Byeongi nagesseoyo.
examples.translation: It's cold out, but you didn't wear a coat. You might get sick.

examples.sentence: 친구를 만나기로 했는데, 비가 와서 계획이 바뀌었어요.
examples.romanization: Chingureul mannagiro haetneunde, biga waseo gyehoegi bakkwieosseoyo.
examples.translation: I was supposed to meet a friend, but it rained, so the plan changed.

examples.sentence: 오늘 공부를 많이 했는데 여전히 이해가 안 가요.
examples.romanization: Oneul gongbureul manhi haetneunde yeojeonhi ihaega an gayo.
examples.translation: I studied a lot today, but I still don't understand.

examples.sentence: 그가 웃었는데, 알고 보니 나한테 화가 나 있었어요.
examples.romanization: Geuga useotneunde, algo boni nahante hwaga na isseosseoyo.
examples.translation: He smiled, but it turned out he was actually angry with me.

title: ~는지 알다/모르다 [neunji alda/moreuda] (Know/don't know whether)
shortExplanation: Used to express knowing or not knowing whether something is or will be the case.
longExplanation: The '~는지 알다/모르다' structure is used to indicate whether the speaker (or someone else) knows or doesn't know a particular fact or circumstance. It can also appear in questions to ask if someone knows about a certain situation.

examples.sentence: 그가 학교에 갔는지 알아요?
examples.romanization: Geuga hakgyoe gatneunji arayo?
examples.translation: Do you know if he went to school?

examples.sentence: 저는 그녀가 아직 사랑하는지 모르겠어요.
examples.romanization: Jeoneun geunyeoga ajik saranghaneunji moreugesseoyo.
examples.translation: I don't know if she still loves (me or someone).

examples.sentence: 우리가 이길 수 있는지 알아요?
examples.romanization: Uriga igil su inneunji arayo?
examples.translation: Do you know if we can win?

examples.sentence: 너가 그의 생일을 기억하는지 모르겠어요.
examples.romanization: Neoga geuui saengireul gieokhaneunji moreugesseoyo.
examples.translation: I don't know if you remember his birthday.

title: ~는지라 [neunjira] (Because, since)
shortExplanation: Used to indicate the reason or cause ('because', 'since').
longExplanation: '~는지라 [neunjira]' emphasizes that the condition in the first clause is the reason or cause for the following situation. It can carry a nuance that the cause is somewhat pressing or unavoidable, functioning like 'because' or 'since'.

examples.sentence: 그녀가 너무 열심히 공부하는지라 숙제도 항상 완벽하게 해요.
examples.romanization: Geunyeoga neomu yeolsimhi gongbuhaneunjira sukjedo hangsang wanbyeokhage haeyo.
examples.translation: Because she studies so hard, she always does her homework perfectly.

examples.sentence: 날씨가 너무 추운지라 학교에 가고 싶지 않아.
examples.romanization: Nalssiga neomu chuunjira hakgyoe gago sipji ana.
examples.translation: Since it's so cold, I don't want to go to school.

examples.sentence: 아기가 아프는지라 온 밤을 잠을 이루지 못했습니다.
examples.romanization: Agiga apeuneunjira on bameul jameul iruji mothaetseumnida.
examples.translation: Because the baby was sick, I couldn't sleep all night.

examples.sentence: 이번 주에 일이 많아서 너무 바쁜지라 휴식할 시간이 전혀 없었어요.
examples.romanization: Ibeon jue iri manaseo neomu bappeunjira hyusikhal sigani jeonhyeo eopseosseoyo.
examples.translation: I was so busy this week due to having a lot of work, so I had no time to rest.

title: ~다가 [daga] (While doing, was doing but)
shortExplanation: Connects two actions, indicating the first action was ongoing but got interrupted or changed by the second action.
longExplanation: '~다가' shows that one action or event was in progress when another action or situation intervened. It often implies that the second action wasn’t necessarily planned, but it happened and stopped the first action in its tracks.

examples.sentence: 책을 읽다가 잠이 들었어요.
examples.romanization: Chaegeul ilgdaga jami deureosseoyo.
examples.translation: I fell asleep while reading a book.

examples.sentence: 집에 가다가 차가 고장 나서 버스를 타고 왔어요.
examples.romanization: Jibe gadaga chaga gojang naseo beoseureul tago wasseoyo.
examples.translation: On my way home, my car broke down, so I took the bus.

examples.sentence: 밥을 먹다가 친구가 급히 전화해서 다 못 먹었어요.
examples.romanization: Babeul meokdaga chinguga geuphi jeonhwahaeseo da mot meogeosseoyo.
examples.translation: While I was eating, my friend suddenly called, so I couldn’t finish my meal.

examples.sentence: 공부하다가 갑자기 나가야 했어요, 부장님이 오셔서요.
examples.romanization: Gongbuhadaga gapjagi nagaya haesseoyo, bujangnimi osyeoseoyo.
examples.translation: I was studying, but I had to leave suddenly because my boss arrived.

title: ~다가는 [daganeun] (If continue doing)
shortExplanation: Expresses a potential negative outcome if a certain action continues.
longExplanation: The pattern '~다가는' warns about a negative result or consequence if the preceding action persists. It’s used to caution someone: 'If you keep doing X, then Y (bad result) will happen.'

examples.sentence: 너는 계속 이렇게 늦게까지 일하다가는 몸이 망가져 버릴 거야.
examples.romanization: Neoneun gyesok ireoke neutgekkaji ilhadaganeun momi manggajyeo beoril geoya.
examples.translation: If you keep working this late, your health will suffer.

examples.sentence: 점심시간에 밥 대신 커피만 마시다가는 건강에 문제가 생길 거예요.
examples.romanization: Jeomsim sigane bap daesin keopiman masidaganeun geongange munjega saenggil geoyeyo.
examples.translation: If you keep drinking only coffee instead of eating lunch, you'll have health problems.

examples.sentence: 우리가 이렇게 자주 충돌하다가는 이 관계는 오래가지 못할 거야.
examples.romanization: Uriga ireoke jaju chungdolhadaganeun i gwangyeneun oraegaji mothal geoya.
examples.translation: If we keep having conflicts so often, this relationship won’t last long.

examples.sentence: 매일 밤 늦게 잠들다가는 아침에 일어나기 힘들어질 거야.
examples.romanization: Maeil bam neutge jamdeuldaganeun achime ireonagi himdeureojil geoya.
examples.translation: If you keep going to bed late every night, it will be hard to get up in the morning.

title: ~다가도 [dagado] (Even though was doing)
shortExplanation: Indicates that an unexpected or sudden change occurred while in the middle of doing something.
longExplanation: '~다가도' is used when something disrupts or abruptly changes an action that was in progress. It conveys a nuance of surprise or sudden shift, differing from what was initially expected to happen.

examples.sentence: 나는 집에 가다가도 갑자기 비가 많이 와서 우산을 샀어요.
examples.romanization: Naneun jibe gadagado gapjagi biga mani waseo usaneul sasseoyo.
examples.translation: Even though I was on my way home, it suddenly started raining a lot, so I bought an umbrella.

examples.sentence: 그는 공부하다가도 친구가 영화를 보자고 하면 바로 그만두고 영화관에 가요.
examples.romanization: Geuneun gongbuhadagado chinguga yeonghwareul bojago hamyeon baro geumandugo yeonghwagwane gayo.
examples.translation: Even if he’s studying, if his friend suggests watching a movie, he immediately stops and goes to the cinema.

examples.sentence: 주인공이 결승전을 이기다가도 마지막에 실수를 해서 패배했어요.
examples.romanization: Juingongi gyeolseungjeoneul igidagado majimage silsureul haeseo paebaehaesseoyo.
examples.translation: Even though the main character was winning the final, he made a mistake at the end and lost.

examples.sentence: 우리는 피크닉을 가다가도 갑자기 날씨가 안 좋아져서 집으로 돌아왔어요.
examples.romanization: Urineun pikeunikeul gadagado gapjagi nalssiga an joajyeoseo jibeuro dolawasseoyo.
examples.translation: We were on our way to a picnic, but the weather suddenly got bad, so we went back home.

title: ~다니 [dani] (Exclamation, surprise)
shortExplanation: Used to express exclamation, surprise, disbelief, or shock.
longExplanation: '~다니 [dani]' conveys strong emotional reaction—amazement, incredulity, or shock—when hearing or realizing something. It's similar to saying 'I can't believe that...' or 'Really?!' in English. It can appear in direct or reported speech.
formation: Verb + 아/어/여 + 다니 / Adjective stem + 다니

examples.sentence: 네가 그녀와 결혼하려고 한다니, 정말 믿을 수 없어!
examples.romanization: Nega geunyeowa gyeolhonharyeogo handani, jeongmal mideul su eopseo!
examples.translation: You're going to marry her? I really can't believe it!

examples.sentence: 내가 이렇게 중요한 프로젝트를 맡게 될 줄이라니, 정말 놀라워!
examples.romanization: Naega ireohge jungyohan peurojekteureul matge doel jurirani, jeongmal nollawo!
examples.translation: I'm really surprised that I ended up being in charge of such an important project!

examples.sentence: 내일 시험이 있다니, 왜 아무도 말해 주지 않았지?
examples.romanization: Naeil siheomi itdani, wae amudo malhae juji anhatji?
examples.translation: There's a test tomorrow? Why didn’t anyone tell me?

examples.sentence: 그가 이런 일을 할 줄 알았다니, 나는 정말 깜짝 놀랐어!
examples.romanization: Geuga ireon ireul hal jul alatdani, naneun jeongmal kkamjjak nollasseo!
examples.translation: I'm really shocked that he would do such a thing!
